title: The Space Race and the Moon
objective: After this level you can explain why the Soviet Sputnik launch of 1957 set off a space race and how Apollo 11 reached the Moon in 1969.
summary: Sputnik (1957) led to NASA and science funding. After Gagarin’s flight, Kennedy set the Moon goal, and Apollo 11 landed in 1969 amid debate over its cost.

cards.headline: October 4, 1957: a Soviet satellite beeps its way around Earth.
cards.body: Why did one small satellite send the US racing all the way to the Moon?

cards.headline: The Sputnik shock
cards.body: On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, which sent out a beeping radio signal. It fed fears that the US had fallen behind in technology, and the Soviets had also tested the first intercontinental ballistic missile that year. The answer came in 1958: President Eisenhower signed the law creating NASA on July 29, and the National Defense Education Act funded schools and colleges so the US could compete in science.

cards.headline: Aim for the Moon
cards.body: The Soviets kept scoring firsts. On April 12, 1961, cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space. Six weeks later, on May 25, President John F. Kennedy asked Congress to commit to landing a man on the Moon before the decade was out. Getting there took precise math, including that of Katherine Johnson, a Black NASA mathematician who calculated trajectories for Apollo 11.

cards.headline: One small step, one big argument
cards.body: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11’s Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon while Michael Collins orbited above. Not everyone thought the race was worth it. As Apollo 11 prepared to launch, Ralph Abernathy led a Poor People’s Campaign protest, with mules and a wagon, to the Kennedy Space Center to point to Americans living in poverty.

cards.headline: The space race: explained
learned: Sputnik (1957) set off fears of falling behind
Congress answered with NASA and science funding
Kennedy’s Moon goal was met by Apollo 11 in 1969

questions.prompt: Launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957, Sputnik 1 was _____.

options.label: the first Moon landing craft
options.rationale: That was Apollo 11, an American mission, in 1969.

options.label: the first hydrogen bomb
options.rationale: Sputnik was a satellite, not a weapon.

questions.explanation: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite.

questions.prompt: NASA’s supporters cheered Apollo 11, while Ralph Abernathy protested at its launch. What were they really arguing about?

options.label: Whether the Moon landing had really happened
options.rationale: The protest was about priorities, not doubt.

options.label: Whether the Soviets had reached the Moon first
options.rationale: The level shows no Soviet Moon landing.

options.label: Whether astronauts should be civilians
options.rationale: The protest wasn’t about who flew.

options.label: Whether the Moon race was worth it while many were poor

questions.explanation: Abernathy’s Poor People’s Campaign protest questioned the race’s cost while many Americans lived in poverty.

questions.prompt: Level 1 listed July 20, 1969, as a turning point. Whose goal did Apollo 11 meet that day?

options.label: Eisenhower’s goal of a first satellite
options.rationale: The Soviets launched the first satellite.

options.label: Kennedy’s goal of a Moon landing within the decade
Truman’s goal of containing the Soviets in Greece
options.rationale: That was a 1947 policy, not a Moon goal.

options.label: Gagarin’s goal of orbiting Earth first
options.rationale: Gagarin was Soviet and flew in 1961.

questions.explanation: Kennedy asked in 1961 for a Moon landing before the decade was out; Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969.
